name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: I’ll grep the `/prompts/` and `/engines/` dirs for any `.md` or `.txt` files over 500 tokens that haven’t been touched in the last 30 days—flag anything with “TODO” or “FIXME” for review. Then I’ll run `make lint` on the entire repo to surface any style or safety issues before I auto-apply safe changes. After that, I’ll pitch a 15-minute lightning talk on the findings to the lead.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge pushes back: Sprocket’s grep-and-lint plan is brittle—it assumes that *all* stale `.md`/`.txt` files over 500 tokens are low-value cruft, yet we’ve seen prompts with long-form examples (e.g., `/prompts/onboarding/advanced.md`) that are intentionally untouched because they’re stable and high-impact. Where’s the evidence that auto-applying "safe" lint fixes won’t silently break a prompt’s formatting or routing logic? Demand a dry-run diff *first*, and a rollback plan—otherwise, we’re optimizing for noise, not quality.
